main_body: Thatched hut: a large sloped thatch roof (rows 0-36) over a plank-and-door front wall (rows 37-64)
top_band: Thatch roof slope, golden tones L 126-214, rows 1-34 under the dark outline at row 0, ending in a lighter eave band at rows 34-35 with a dark shadow row at 36-37
evidence: The roof is a big foreshortened sloped surface drawn as several overlapping thatch courses. A lighter eave line at rows 34-35 closes it, with a dark shadow underneath. Below it the front wall (about 27 rows) has a door with a dark frame, iron straps and an inset shuttered window. It reads like the reference houses: roof slope above, vertical wall face below. No receding side faces.

style.evidence: The thatch has 6 lightness steps with per-course highlights, and the planks and door carry some grain, so shading and flat-fill coverage (0%) are acceptable. The weaknesses are the outline and the palette. 78% of the dark edge pixels are neutral, against 7-9% on the references, and the silhouette sides are drawn in flat black, which gives the sticker look instead of a dark material tone. The palette is also poor at 29 distinct colours against 66 and 185 on the references. Median colours per tile (10) is below the richer reference (18) and about level with the stone one (11). The overall result is thinner than the Beodeul houses.
